rationale: Roberts is likely to keep the opinion narrow and institutional, adopting a whole-text/surplusage reading that preserves § 7609(a)-(b) notice for third-party summonses lacking a clear legal nexus to collecting from the assessed taxpayer, while avoiding constitutional questions. Alito likely writes (possibly joined by Kavanaugh) to defend the government’s broader ordinary-meaning/anti-dissipation reading and to emphasize Powell as an adequate safeguard.
